newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cardoso's popularity recovers in new Brazil poll.
newsitem.headline: Cardoso's popularity recovers in new Brazil poll.

text.p: The approval ratings of Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and of his government have recovered after a recent slump, a poll published Sunday said.
A survey by private polling company Brasmarket and published in magazine Isto E found 78.9 percent of 2,974 people interviewed thought Cardoso was doing either an excellent, good or competent job.
The poll, the first since Congress approved a bill allowing the president to run for re-election next year, found 71.2 percent of respondents approved of his government.
An identical poll carried out by Brasmarket for Isto E exactly a year ago gave Cardoso a 67.9 percent personal approval rating while 58.8 percent approved of his government.
Sunday's poll also contrasted with other, more recent surveys which detected a fall in the popularity of Cardoso and his government after a corruption scandal in Congress and other problems.
In May, a poll by IBOPE, another research company, showed the president's approval rating at an all-time low of 50 percent.

The latest survey, carried out on June 12, found unemployment to be far and away the biggest worry of most Brazilians, with 53.8 percent saying it was their main concern. The cost of living (9.1 percent) and corruption (7.1 percent) followed.
